title: "Reference"
subtitle: "Symbols, functions, data, and sources"
---

## Symbols

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $\mathbf{y}(t)$, $y$ | state of the crop; here biomass (t/ha) |
| $\mathbf{u}(t) = (u_1, \dots, u_m)$ | environmental drivers, standardised |
| $\theta_j(\mathbf{y}, \mathbf{u})$ | candidate function $j$ of the library |
| $\boldsymbol{\theta}$ | vector of all candidate functions |
| $\boldsymbol{\xi}$ | coefficient vector |
| $\dot y_i \approx (y_i - y_{i-1}) / \Delta t$, $\dot{\mathbf{y}}$ | growth rate of day $i$ by the one-day difference (centered at the middle of the day), and the vector of growth rates |
| $\boldsymbol{\Theta}$, $\Theta_{ij}$ | matrix of the library evaluated on the days used (rows), $\Theta_{ij} = \theta_j(\mathbf{y}_i, \mathbf{u}_i)$; the design matrix |
| $K$ | number of candidate functions |

## Functions

All functions are in `R/functions.R` (R) and `python/dgxe.py` (Python), with the same names and arguments.

| Function | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `make_drivers(weather)` | standardised drivers `U[year, day, driver]` |
| `make_library(drv, degree, pairs)` | library `Theta[year, day, term]` |
| `extra_terms(weather, exprs)`, `bind_terms(Theta, extra)` | extra library terms from expressions of the raw weather |
| `with_traits(weather, traj, genotype, vars)` | adds measured states (`"LAI"`, `"biomass"`) to the weather as day series, so they can be drivers or appear in expressions |
| `make_trajectories(traj, drv, var)` | response `Y[genotype, year, day]` |
| `make_design(Theta, tr, genotype)` | design matrix `Theta` (library of the days used) and growth rates `dy` (one-day differences) |
| `fit_ols`, `fit_ridge`, `fit_lasso`, `fit_enet`, `fit_subset`, `fit_stlsq` | fitting methods `fit(Theta, dy)` |
| `simulate(coef, U, y0)` | solution of the fitted equation with an ODE solver |
| `cross_validate(Theta, tr, fit)` | leave-one-year-out predictions |
| `make_design_states(Theta, trs, genotype, drivers, degree, pairs, feedback)` | design with state terms (`state_terms`) and one column of `dy` per modelled state; `trs` is a list of trajectory sets, one per state |
| `simulate_states(coef, U, y0, terms)` | solution of the coupled system; years that blow up are returned as `NA` |
| `cross_validate_states(Theta, trs, fit, genotypes, drivers, degree, pairs, feedback)` | leave-one-year-out predictions of the (coupled) model, one `P` per state, and the number of diverged years |
| `evaluate(P, tr)` | trajectory, fixed-day and maturity RMSE |
| `ale_curve(rate, Z, j)` | accumulated local effect of driver `j` |
| `rank_scores(Pd, Yd)` | ranking metrics |

The R and Python versions differ only in conventions: R uses `TRUE`/`FALSE` and `1:n` indexing, Python uses `True`/`False`, zero-based indexing and the attribute syntax `tr.Y` instead of `tr$Y`.

## Data

APSIM wheat simulations at Narrabri (New South Wales, Australia): 199 genotypes, 31 years (1983 to 2013), daily. Columns are described in [Data](02-data.qmd). Files are in `data/`.

## Sources

- Preprint: Verburg, C., Heinlein, A., van Eeuwijk, F. and Budko, N. (2026). *Physiology-Informed Sparse Identification of Dynamic Crop Models*. [arXiv:2610.18920](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.18920v1).
- Bustos-Korts, D. et al. (2019). From QTLs to adaptation landscapes: using genotype-to-phenotype models to characterize G×E over time. *Frontiers in Plant Science* 10, 1540. doi:10.3389/fpls.2019.01540. Data: [figshare](https://figshare.com/articles/dataset/24843705).
- Brunton, S. L., Proctor, J. L. and Kutz, J. N. (2016). Discovering governing equations from data by sparse identification of nonlinear dynamical systems. *PNAS* 113(15), 3932–3937.
- Friedman, J., Hastie, T. and Tibshirani, R. (2010). Regularization paths for generalized linear models via coordinate descent. *Journal of Statistical Software* 33(1), 1–22 (`glmnet`).
- Lumley, T. and Miller, A. `leaps`: regression subset selection. R package.
- Apley, D. W. and Zhu, J. (2020). Visualizing the effects of predictor variables in black box supervised learning models. *Journal of the Royal Statistical Society B* 82(4), 1059–1086.
